name: Maaseiah
overview: Maaseiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of King Ahaz. His mention is concise, with no additional notes expanding on his life or deeds beyond his royal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Maaseiah means 'Yahweh is a refuge,' reflecting a meaningful declaration of God's protective nature. This proper name is noted in 2 Chronicles 28:7 but was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Maaseiah as the son of Ahaz, the king of Judah. No further family relationships are documented beyond this direct paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Maaseiah's significance in the biblical narrative primarily stems from his royal heritage as the son of King Ahaz. This connection situates him within the Davidic line, an important lineage in God's redemptive plan. Although details about his personal actions are not provided, his mention in 2 Chronicles underscores his place in the historical record of Judah's monarchy.
